architecture: Two agencies, each with its own hub + secondary-hub, cross-linked at one shared-building station. National Rail: hub lock Manchester Piccadilly (MAN, 14 platforms, all six TOCs), secondary hub Manchester Victoria (MCV, 6 platforms, Northern + TransPennine Express only) — reuses the Thames Valley/Solent/West of England hub+secondary-hub pattern. Metrolink: hub lock St Peter's Square (all 8 lines converge, Zone 1), secondary hub Manchester Victoria. Manchester Victoria is built once as a single stationGroup with doNotGroup: true between its Metrolink and National Rail layers (same shape as Sheffield Station in South Yorkshire's pack). Manchester Piccadilly (NR) and Piccadilly Gardens (Metrolink) are built as two separate stationGroups, doNotGroup: true between them — a walk-link pair (~100m, 5-10 min), NOT a shared-building interchange the way Victoria is. This departs from the oracle report's headline C2/C3 point 4 ('hub lock: Victoria') in favour of the report's own platform/operator-count facts (line 22); see direction-model-memo.md for full reasoning and open item 1 for Tim.

ARCHITECTURE: two agencies, two hub+secondary-hub pairs, cross-linked at Manchester Victoria. See top-level 'architecture' field and direction-model-memo.md for full reasoning, including the departure from the oracle report's headline C2/C3 point 4 recommendation.

Metrolink modes v1: light rail, line+terminus model, SCHEDULE-ONLY (no confirmed real-time feed — TfGM developer portal deprecated, no new keys issued). This is a genuine feed-status gap, same kind as South Yorkshire's Supertram/SYFTL gap, not the standard National Rail account block. Do not conflate the two in downstream QA notes.

National Rail modes v1: heavy rail, destination-board model (not line+terminus). BLOCKED pending DARWIN_LDB_TOKEN — see coverageGaps. Build the catalog/adapter normally per Nico's report; do not wire the token until it exists.

Hub lock (National Rail): Manchester Piccadilly (MAN CRS), 14 platforms, all six TOCs (Northern, Avanti West Coast, TransPennine Express, CrossCountry, East Midlands Railway, Transport for Wales). Secondary hub (National Rail): Manchester Victoria (MCV CRS), 6 platforms, Northern + TransPennine Express only.
Hub lock (Metrolink): St Peter's Square, all 8 lines converge (Zone 1 city centre, most-used stop on the network). Secondary hub (Metrolink): Manchester Victoria.

doNotGroup: Manchester Victoria Metrolink tram platforms (4) vs National Rail platforms (6) — same building, escalator/lift connect, separate operators/infrastructure. Same shape as Sheffield Station (South Yorkshire) and Nottingham Station (East Midlands).

doNotGroup: Manchester Piccadilly (National Rail) vs Piccadilly Gardens (Metrolink) — ~100m apart, 5-10 min walk, undercroft vs street-level main platforms. NOT a shared-building case; closer to Bradford Forster Square/Bradford Interchange (West Yorkshire) than to Victoria.

No Metrolink stop at Stockport — the earlier 'two Stockports' hazard was an error (7 Sep 2026). Manchester Metrolink has never served Stockport; a Stockport extension has only been proposed. See docs/jim-brief-net-toton-lane-and-stockport-tram.md.

Neither is treated as authoritative here — flagged for Tim/Nico to resolve against a live Darwin response before either pack's Walsden CRS is used in an adapter. See hazard-pack.md.
